name: Curly girl method
lead: The Curly Girl Method (CGM) is a haircare routine for wavy, curly and coily hair that avoids sulfate shampoos, silicones, heat and brushes, and emphasizes conditioner washing, moisture and finger detangling. People use it to get more defined, less frizzy curls and a more consistent curl pattern.

It was popularized by stylist Lorraine Massey in her 2001 book Curly Girl: The Handbook, and spread widely through social media and curly-hair communities. Many followers report softer, more defined curl patterns after a transition period.

General references on hair care describe the ideas the method builds on: conditioners reduce friction between strands, which eases detangling and reduces combing damage, and co-washing means using a cleansing conditioner instead of shampoo, mainly for dry, sensitive or textured hair.[1] Textured hair is described as needing more moisture than straight hair and benefiting from low heat.[2] No clinical trials of the full method were found.

chain: Remove harsh cleansers, silicones and brushing
Curls look defined with less frizz
angle.text: Followers use the routine to define their natural curl pattern and reduce frizz. The look is visible within weeks as hair adapts.

infobox: Sulfate-free cleansing, conditioner, finger detangling, no heat, gel cast

paras: Core rules commonly listed are cleansing with sulfate-free shampoo or conditioner, avoiding silicones and drying alcohols, detangling with fingers or a wide-tooth comb, drying with a soft cotton shirt or microfiber towel instead of a rough towel, and avoiding heat. Styling gel is used to form a cast that is scrunched out when dry.

sections.h: How the rules relate to hair science
paras: Hair-conditioner references explain that cationic surfactants bind to hair and smooth the cuticle, that silicones such as dimethicone form a film that lowers friction and adds shine but can build up, and that acidic ingredients reduce frizz by tightening the cuticle.[1] Those same references describe co-washing as suited to textured hair and suggest alternating with a clarifying shampoo to limit buildup, which parallels the transition phase followers describe.[1]

Descriptions of textured hair note that it shrinks when dry, requires more moisture, and is vulnerable to breakage from vigorous dry-combing and prolonged heat, with guidance to limit heat and keep hair moisturized.[2]

Some followers go through a transition phase in which hair feels different as product build-up is removed. Variations exist for low-porosity or fine hair that find the original product guidance too heavy.
Stylists and dermatologists note that some hair types need regular cleansing and that wash frequency suits scalp type; some followers report build-up with heavy conditioners.

timeline.event: Lorraine Massey publishes Curly Girl: The Handbook.

card.summary: A sulfate-free, no-brush routine that helps curly hair keep its shape and moisture for more defined curls.

quick.overview:
The Curly Girl Method is a curly-hair routine built around gentle cleansing, conditioner, no brushes and no heat.

Followers use it to get defined, frizz-free curls.
quick.mechanism: Avoiding strong detergents and mechanical brushing is meant to keep natural oils and moisture in the hair and keep curl clumps intact.
quick.risks: Low risk. Some people get build-up or find the routine too heavy for their hair type.
